name: Combination Skin
description: Combination skin is characterized by a mix of oily and dry areas, typically with an oily T-zone (forehead, nose, chin) and drier cheeks. This skin type can be challenging to manage due to its varying texture and oil production.
symptoms: Mixture of pores and smooth skin areas
Possible breakouts in the oily areas
risk_factors: Hormonal changes during puberty, pregnancy, or menopause

daily_routine.purpose: Remove excess oil and impurities without stripping natural oils from the skin.
Balance skin's pH level and prepare it for better absorption of subsequent products.
Target specific concerns like acne or dehydration.
Provide hydration to dry areas while controlling oil in the T-zone.

natural_remedies: Tea tree oil for acne-prone skin
Green tea to soothe and tighten pores
Aloe vera for its hydrating properties
lifestyle_tips: Wear sunscreen daily to protect against UV damage.
Maintain a balanced diet rich in antioxidants.
Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water.
common_myths: Combination skin can be fully controlled with makeup alone.
Using only oil-free products is sufficient for managing combination skin.
when_to_consult_doctor: If breakouts persist despite proper care or if you experience severe irritation, redness, or discoloration.
prevention: Regularly exfoliate to prevent clogged pores
Keep the skin hydrated but avoid over-moisturizing oily areas

severity_levels.mild: Occasional breakouts and uneven texture that can be managed with a simple skincare routine.
severity_levels.moderate: More frequent breakouts, visible oiliness in the T-zone, and dry patches on cheeks that may require more targeted treatment.
severity_levels.severe: Persistent skin issues like cystic acne, significant redness, or severe dehydration that need professional intervention.

expert_tips: Use products with a non-greasy formula to avoid clogging pores.
Patch test new products before applying them all over your face.
Consult a dermatologist for personalized advice and treatment plans.
